thread:
incident-bot: P2 alert: continuous-batcher reporting repeated GPU OOMs and driver faults; node paging observed in gpu-pool-2. Auto-created incident thread. thread_ts=1907765432

oncall-ash: Acknowledged. I'll take ownership. What's the immediate customer impact? Any 5xx spike?

deploy-bot: Alert: error-rate(/generate)>5% for 3m. Samples: 502 CUDA error, 500 OOM.

eng-runner: Logs from 14:12 window:
```
E0315 14:12:07 batcher.go:401] pendingQueue.len=1472
E0315 14:12:08 mem.go:77] KV eviction failed: not enough memory
E0315 14:12:09 cuda.go:112] cuBLAS error: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION
panic: runtime: out of memory
```

infra-kate: Node checks: node-gpu-23 and node-gpu-24 flapped Kubelet restarts and dmesg shows oom_killer on nvidia processes. Paging to disk seen at 14:11-14:13.

sre-ben: Immediate plan: 1) divert new /generate traffic off continuous-batcher and onto sync-fallback 2) apply emergency rate cap on the batcher 3) cordon & drain affected nodes 4) enable driver consistency check. Can someone flip the routing?

oncall-ash: Routing change in progress — activating fallback for /generate:sync-lowlatency variant for 20m via console: `redwood route set /generate --policy fallback:sync-low --ttl 20m`. Applying now.

cust-success-lina: Noting: this will degrade latency for some customers. Pulling list of high-traffic tenants now.

eng-runner: Quick check query:
`SELECT tenant_id, count(*) FROM requests WHERE route='/generate' AND ts>now()-15m GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 5;`
Top tenants: tenant-proto, tenant-smb-88, tenant-enterprise-A. I'll draft notices.

infra-kate: Running cordon/drain on node-gpu-23: `kubectl cordon node-gpu-23 && kubectl drain node-gpu-23 --ignore-daemonsets --force` starting. Will reprovision nodes with baseline NVIDIA driver 525.89.

sre-ben: Patching batcher config map to enforce emergency caps:
```
continuousBatcher:
  maxPendingBatches: 200
  maxBatchSize: 64
  rejectOnEvictionFailure: true
```
Applying and restarting only on healthy AZs.

oncall-ash: After routing switch, error-rate fell from 6.1% -> 0.8% and queue depth dropped from ~1400 to ~60 in 45s. Latency p95 increased ~300ms as expected.

eng-runner: Root cause hypothesis: when KV cache eviction returns errors under memory pressure, the batcher did not propagate backpressure and kept growing the pending queue. That eventually exhausted GPU memory and triggered illegal-instruction when driver state got inconsistent during OOM.

sre-ben: Hotfix idea: short-circuit pending enqueue when eviction fails and return 429, plus a circuit-breaker that tears down oversized batches. Can we ship a canary?

eng-runner: Pushing a canary with the guard now to canary nodes. Code change: on eviction failure -> increment metric eviction_failure_count; if >1 within 10s -> reject new batch with 429 and log.

infra-kate: Reimaging completes on node-gpu-23/24; drivers synced. Uncordoning node-gpu-23 at 14:42, small traffic ramp with split routing: `redwood route split /generate continuous-batcher=20%,sync-low=80% --duration 5m`.

oncall-ash: No new CUDA errors after 10m ramp on reintroduced nodes. Canary shows guard fired 3 times and prevented queue growth. Promoting hotfix cluster-wide.

cust-success-lina: Customer notifications sent to tenant-enterprise-A and tenant-proto. They acknowledged and asked for estimated full restore time. I provided ETA 45m and will share postmortem link later.

sre-ben: Closing note: adjust alerting thresholds: queue_depth > 250 -> page P1; eviction_failure_rate > 0.25% sustained -> P1. Also add a heartbeat for driver version drift.

oncall-ash: Incident marked resolved at 14:55. Leaving fallback in place until hotfix verification completes (additional 30m). Postmortem assigned to eng-runner, infra-kate, and sre-ben. Will post to #incidents when ready. Thanks everyone.

incident-bot: Incident closed by oncall-ash. Summary: continuous-batcher queue growth due to KV eviction failures leading to GPU OOMs and driver faults. Mitigations: routing fallback, emergency caps, node reimage/driver sync, and hotfix guard to reject on eviction failure.
